title: Texas's 33rd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Texas's 33rd Congressional District pits former U.S. Rep. Colin Allred (D) against Republican nominee Patrick Gillespie. The seat is open after incumbent Rep. Marc Veasey (D) retired following the 2025 Republican-led mid-decade redistricting that substantially redrew the district's boundaries. The new map created a heavily Democratic-leaning district (Cook PVI D+18) that triggered an unusual Democratic primary between Allred and the incumbent who succeeded him, Rep. Julie Johnson, which Allred won in a May 2026 runoff. The race is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report, though Allred's past statewide loss and the district's new boundaries make this a closely watched contest in the battle for control of the U.S. House.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls were found for TX-33 as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D.'

candidates.name: Colin Allred
candidates.summary: Colin Allred is a former U.S. Representative for Texas's 32nd District (2019–2025), a civil rights attorney, and a former NFL linebacker for the Tennessee Titans. He won the Democratic nomination for TX-33 by defeating incumbent Rep. Julie Johnson in a contentious May 2026 primary runoff, after briefly launching and then abandoning a second U.S. Senate bid. Allred was first elected to Congress in 2018 by unseating 11-term Republican Pete Sessions and was the 2024 Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, losing to incumbent Ted Cruz.

candidates.name: Patrick David Gillespie
candidates.summary: Patrick Gillespie is the Republican nominee for Texas's 33rd Congressional District. He works for UPS Supply Chain Solutions and has run for this seat previously in 2024, losing to incumbent Rep. Marc Veasey. Gillespie advanced from a four-candidate Republican primary in March 2026 and won the Republican primary runoff on May 26, 2026. His campaign emphasizes border security, reducing the national debt, combating fentanyl trafficking, and opposing what he describes as Marxist influences in American institutions.
